then.prompt: Remove a steam counter from Backup Protocol: RED? (Otherwise it is destroyed.)

_comment: The printed **Crank** keyword is engine-side from the card DB keywords field (ability_keywords.crank = CR 8.3.29 'as this enters the arena, you may remove a steam counter from it; if you do, gain an action point') and is deliberately NOT authored here. The sentence below it ('This enters the arena with a steam counter. At the start of your turn, destroy this unless you remove a steam counter from it.') is a SEPARATE static ability per CR (the Golden Cog entry lists Crank AND that sentence as two abilities), so it IS authored: (1) entry counter as TRIGGERED ON_ENTER_PLAY + PUT_COUNTER (shipped arc/teklo_core_blue.json pattern; Zone.add dispatches ON_ENTER_PLAY on arena entry, and 'enters with' vs 'immediately after' is observationally equivalent here); effect_put_counter writes the card-level tally that COUNTER_GTE reads, and also the player-level (slug, zone, kind) tally that engine crank() consumes - so cranking the counter off on entry works and the upkeep then correctly finds none. (2) Upkeep: START_OF_TURN reaches only the turn player's items/permanents (engine._dsl_start_of_turn_listener -> _dsl_permanent_zones includes player.items), which is exactly 'your turn'. The gate sits on CONDITIONAL's 'when' - NOT ability-level conditions or MAY-level conditions, either of which would skip the destroy along with the removal. With a counter: MAY offers remove-or-destroy, declining runs MAY's else = DESTROY_SELF. With zero counters (cranked away on entry): the CONDITIONAL else destroys directly, so the item can never survive an upkeep it should not. (3) Instant: the {r}{r} is card-level activation_cost=2 (DSL-authoritative; NOT repeated as a PAY_RESOURCES cost, which would double-charge); 'destroy this' is the ability-level DESTROY_SELF cost - a cost, so it gates legality and _apply_activate pays it before effects run. INSTANT timing gives priority-window activation; play._add_hero_dsl_activations offers item abilities (ACTIVATABLE_ABILITY_TYPES includes INSTANT). Triage suggested SEARCH_GRAVEYARD, but its handler reads only filter_types/slug_contains/name_contains - no colour or class parameter - so it could not express 'red Mechanologist'; instead RETURN_TO_HAND takes a canonical object target over GRAVEYARD (_object_zone_cards supports it) filtered by CARD_IS_COLOR red / CARD_IS_CLASS Mechanologist / CARD_IS_TYPE Attack (checks types AND subtypes, so attack actions match while attack reactions do not). The controller chooses among matches at resolution; no match returns an empty pool and nothing moves (fail to find, matching the release-note edge case). Unlike the BANISH+MOVE_REF route used by the blue/yellow sibling drafts, this path moves the card graveyard -> hand directly with no banished-zone transit.
